zero_source_forward_star.setup: Let P_N=|Omega_N^+><Omega_N^+|+|Omega_N^-><Omega_N^-|, Q_N=1-P_N, k_N P_N=P_N k_N=0, and k_N restricted to Q_N >=Gamma_N Q_N on the exact full onsite oscillator. Assume Gamma_N=min sigma(k_N restricted to Q_N)>0 is an attained eigenvalue, as it is for the compact-resolvent Q3 onsite operator. Let s_N have eigenvalues +1 and -1 on Omega_N^+ and Omega_N^-, respectively, and vanish on Q_N, and let J_N>0. On each positive cubic edge e=(x,x+e_i), put h_(e,N)^0=(k_(x,N)+k_(x+e_i,N))/6+J_N(1-s_(x,N)s_(x+e_i,N)). Group the three positive edges at x into h_(x,N)^0.
zero_source_forward_star.exact_kernel_and_gap: The kernel of h_(x,N)^0 is exactly the span of the two four-site products (Omega_N^+)^(tensor 4) and (Omega_N^-)^(tensor 4). Its exact attained positive spectral threshold is g_(star,N)^0=min{2J_N,Gamma_N/6+J_N}. A one-neighbour low-label disagreement attains 2J_N and one high neighbour attains Gamma_N/6+J_N.
zero_source_forward_star.large_N_corridor: Along the registered v1.9 corridor, g_(star,N)^0 tends to 16. After enlarging N_1, J_N>=1 and g_(star,N)^0>=g_0=1.
zero_source_forward_star.grouped_relative_form: If every inherited edge residual obeys |V_(e,N)(psi,psi)|<=alpha_N h_(e,N)^0(psi,psi)+beta_N||psi||^2, then phi_(x,N)=sum_(i=1)^3 V_((x,x+e_i),N) obeys |phi_(x,N)|<=alpha_N h_(x,N)^0+3beta_N||psi||^2. Define H_N(t,h)=sum_x[h_(x,N)^0+t phi_(x,N)]+h sum_x s_(x,N); by the inherited exact edge decomposition H_N(1,0) is the physical zero-source Hamiltonian up to the already declared scalar. After normalization by g_(star,N)^0 the inputs are alpha_N and 3beta_N/g_(star,N)^0.
zero_source_forward_star.conditional_common_radius: Assume constants a_2,b_2>0 depend only on dimension three, the fixed forward-star support/range, and its normalized two-ground-pattern Peierls/local-gap datum, and are independent of onsite dimension, spectral cutoff, N, and the upper reference spectrum. In addition, assume the corresponding parity-equivariant two-phase theorem applies directly to the exact infinite-dimensional form reference, or that its finite-cutoff conclusions pass through a separately assumed cutoff-stable compactness and identification theorem. Whenever alpha<a_2 and beta_prime<b_2, assume this theorem has the declared two-phase conclusion. If alpha_N<=C_alpha N^-2, beta_N<=C_beta N^-3, and g_(star,N)^0>=g_0 for N>=N_1, then every N>=N_*=1+max{N_1,floor(sqrt(C_alpha/a_2)),floor((3C_beta/(g_0 b_2))^(1/3))} enters strictly.
zero_source_forward_star.coexistence_pin: Use the exactly parity-odd bounded probe h sum_x s_(x,N). Parity maps h to -h and the two product energy derivatives differ by 2 per site. Conditional on the common theorem rectangle and its local coexistence graph, the nonzero derivative splitting pins that graph to h=0. At interpolation endpoint t=1 this is the physical zero-source full oscillator.
zero_source_forward_star.boundary: The exact kernel, gap, grouped form bound, and conditional entry reduction are proved. Neither direct full-oscillator applicability nor a cutoff-stable passage theorem nor the dimension/cutoff/N-independent constants a_2,b_2 are proved. Yarotskii's 2006 theorem has finite-dimensional onsite spaces and an existential small radius, so it does not supply these premises. No zero-source two-phase full-oscillator theorem is claimed.

bond_modulation_classification.setup: Let H_x=H_y=L2(R^8), M_s=exp(i s.q_x), B_t=exp(i(c t/hbar)q_x.q_y), c!=0, and beta_t=Ad(B_t) with beta_t(C)=B_t^* C B_t.
bond_modulation_classification.fiber_identity: Under the direct integral over q_y, ||beta_t(A tensor I)-A tensor I||=ess sup_y ||M_((ct/hbar)y)^* A M_((ct/hbar)y)-A|| for A in B(H_x). For t!=0 scaling is a measure-class bijection. The function F_A(s)=||M_s^*AM_s-A|| is lower semicontinuous, so its essential supremum is its supremum.
bond_modulation_classification.classification: For c!=0, beta is point-norm continuous at zero on the cylinder A tensor I if and only if sup_s F_A(s)=0, if and only if A commutes with every M_s, if and only if A belongs to the multiplication MASA L_infinity(R^8). Thus C(beta) intersect (B(H_x) tensor I)=L_infinity(R^8) tensor I.
bond_modulation_classification.scope: This classifies only standard one-site cylinders for the isolated bilinear bond flow, not the full two-site continuous-element algebra. In particular K(H_x tensor H_y) remains continuous, while K(H_x) tensor I is not two-site compact. This strengthens the v2.5 compact-cylinder analysis and does not prove failure of the unsplit exact Q3 dynamics or of a dressed or weaker-topology spatial embedding.

summable_single_toggle_shell_reduction.setup: Let one common unital C-star algebra A carry point-norm C0 automorphism groups alpha_F for finite interaction-label backgrounds F, and let D be a norm-dense unital star-subalgebra. Fix a finite seed support X and assign every interaction label j an integer shell r(j), assigning the finitely many core labels shell zero. Require local finiteness: {j:r(j)<=R} is finite for every R.
summable_single_toggle_shell_reduction.primitive_hypothesis: For every A in D and T>0 there are weights w_j(A,T)>=0 such that, uniformly for every finite intermediate background F not containing j and every t in [-T,T], ||alpha_(F union {j})^t(A)-alpha_F^t(A)||<=w_j(A,T). Put B_r(A,T)=sum_(j:r(j)=r)w_j(A,T) and assume sum_r B_r(A,T)<infinity.
summable_single_toggle_shell_reduction.telescope: If F and G contain every label through shell R, telescope F to F union G and G to F union G in arbitrary orders. Background-uniformity gives sup_(|t|<=T)||alpha_F^t(A)-alpha_G^t(A)||<=sum_(j in F symmetric_difference G)w_j(A,T)<=sum_(r>R)B_r(A,T), which tends to zero.
summable_single_toggle_shell_reduction.conclusion: The full directed net is point-norm Cauchy on D uniformly on compact time intervals for both signs. Isometry and density extend the limits to A; the existing v2.4 bidirectional completion gives one exhaustion-independent point-norm C0 automorphism group with products, stars, group law, inverse, and surjectivity.
summable_single_toggle_shell_reduction.boundary: This is a deterministic sufficient reduction. No summable single-toggle weights are proved for the exact quartic Q3 Hamiltonian. Total-generator temporal smoothing alone does not localize the unbounded boundary-bond commutators and does not verify the premise.

gns_gap_transfer.setup: Let A be unital and let D be a common unital star-core contained in the domains of every delta_n and delta. Let omega_n converge weak-star to omega and delta_n(A) converge in norm to delta(A) for every A in D. Assume each omega_n is invariant under its delta_n-dynamics, so the finite energy form is real. Let delta=d/dt alpha_t at zero for an omega-invariant target point-norm C0 group alpha. Assume liminf Delta_n>=Delta>0 and -i hbar omega_n(A^*delta_n(A))>=Delta_n[omega_n(A^*A)-|omega_n(A)|^2].
gns_gap_transfer.limit_form: Weak-star state convergence and norm convergence of delta_n(A) pass the inequality to -i hbar omega(A^*delta(A))>=Delta[omega(A^*A)-|omega(A)|^2] on D.
gns_gap_transfer.implementation: Assume the target GNS group has positive implementer H, H Omega=0, and -i hbar omega(A^*delta(A))=<pi(A)Omega,H pi(A)Omega>. If C_D={pi(A)Omega-omega(A)Omega:A in D} is a linear form core for H^(1/2) on Omega-perp, form closure gives H restricted to Omega-perp >=Delta. Hence the target GNS ground vector is simple and the GNS gap is at least Delta.
gns_gap_transfer.boundary: This theorem transfers a gap only after target dynamics, local-generator convergence, positivity, the energy identity, and the centered form-core property are established. It proves none of those model-dependent Q3 premises.

finite_gap_state_limit_no_go.fixture: On M2 let omega_n=|0><0| and H_n=n|1><1|. Every state is the same simple ground state and every gap is n>=1. For A=|1><0| and hbar=1, delta_n(A)=i n A, the variance is 1, and -i omega_n(A^*delta_n(A))=n. But ||delta_m(A)-delta_n(A)||=|m-n|, so the local generators are not norm Cauchy and no prescribed target generator is identified.
finite_gap_state_limit_no_go.scope: Weak-star convergence of finite ground states plus a uniform finite-volume gap does not automatically identify the target dynamics or transfer a target GNS gap. This is distinct from the post-hoc direct-sum negative, which concerns combining phasewise systems after reconstruction.

literature_scope.yarotskii_2006: D. A. Yarotskii, Pirogov-Sinai theory for relatively bounded quantum perturbations of classical lattice models, Russian Mathematical Surveys 61:2 (2006), 371-372, DOI 10.1070/RM2006v061n02ABEH004323. This two-phase result is finite-onsite and has an existential small radius; it is scope calibration, not a direct Q3 import. The distinct single-phase infinite-onsite source is Ground states in relatively bounded quantum perturbations of classical lattice systems, Commun. Math. Phys. 261 (2006), 799-819, arXiv:math-ph/0412040.
literature_scope.oscillator_lr: B. Nachtergaele, H. Raz, B. Schlein and R. Sims, arXiv:0712.3820, treats unbounded harmonic coupling plus anharmonic onsite V under V' in L1 and a Fourier first-moment condition; a quartic onsite potential fails that hypothesis. L. Amour, P. Levy-Bruhl and J. Nourrigat, arXiv:0904.2717, uses a subquadratic/Fourier-regular perturbation class. Neither closes exact quartic Q3.
literature_scope.gap_calibration: B. Nachtergaele, R. Sims and A. Young, arXiv:2010.15337, obtains GNS gaps for bounded-spin frustration-free/LTQO systems. J. Henheik and S. Teufel, arXiv:2012.15238, explicitly assumes gapped finite volumes generate the same infinite-volume dynamics. These calibrate the missing bridge and are not imported as exact Q3 theorems.
